- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in the recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 30d horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 2–4% for 3–7 day horizon.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.20) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates the 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment <0.30.
- For 30d forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent 3-day average or add 1–2% upward bias.
- When sentiment peaks near the end of history (e.g., last 3 days), model often fails to capture sentiment-driven reversal; reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment peaks within last 3 days.
